purpose: Continue observational design validation of the no-new-subscription path. No accepted runtime edits or target mutation.
status: IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS REFINED — ACT-045 REMAINS OPEN

new_observations.finding: Node request close is not client-response disconnect.
new_observations.evidence: The naive incoming.close hook rejected a completed valid upload with HTTP 400 and zero dispatches. Guarding incomplete uploads and using response.close with !writableFinished allowed one completed execution.
new_observations.requirement: Abort on incomplete upload or prematurely closed response; do not abort on every completed incoming request. Preserve one registered terminal owner beyond the socket lifetime.

new_observations.finding: Client disconnection does not have to lose terminal persistence on a persistent host.
new_observations.evidence: Both architectures recorded socket close, execution abort and one delayed unknown write, in that order. The 120 ms write completed after socket close. Simulated storage only.
new_observations.requirement: Track terminalWork separately from the response pump. During controlled shutdown stop admission, drain owned requests and terminal writes, then close the database pool. Abrupt process loss is still not a persistence guarantee.

new_observations.finding: Upstream activity is not a public transport keepalive.
new_observations.evidence: Unchanged Nova filtered upstream comment and empty-choice frames; the public reader remained pending until content arrived. Existing RelayChatTransport also discards comments and resets idle time only on data.
new_observations.requirement: After authorized SSE headers, the Node response adapter emits bounded comment keepalives (15 seconds is the previously probed design value). Comments must not reset inference TTFT/idle/wall timers, bypass authorization, reveal infrastructure, or signify completion. Serialize comment and data writes with backpressure and stop the timer on every exit.

new_observations.finding: The upstream byte cap is not a safe copy for a client wire cap.
new_observations.evidence: 680088 upstream bytes projected to 3240195 public SSE bytes across 20002 delivered chunks, with terminal completed. This contains many empty deltas; it is synthetic adversarial evidence, not observed production traffic.
new_observations.requirement: Retain only allowlisted text plus minimal request/terminal state. Bound UTF-8 answer bytes, pending event bytes and total wire/event overhead separately. Derive and test wire/frame limits against the largest accepted projection; do not claim the exact new limits are accepted yet.

new_observations.finding: A finish-reason frame alone does not authorize complete-answer success.
new_observations.evidence: A simulated terminal storage failure attempted one completed write, returned sanitized outcome_unconfirmed and emitted no DONE. No second write or dispatch was attempted.
new_observations.requirement: The client requires a valid stop/length finish reason followed by DONE; EOF, abort, malformed frames or an error yields unconfirmed output without automatic POST replay. A failed client delivery does not rewrite an already completed server record.

new_observations.finding: The complete resource boundary can reuse existing modules, but its dependencies and authority placement need deliberate packaging.
new_observations.evidence: inference bundles from two source files; executor from nine; repository from four plus pg. Selected CORS/header exports retain broader framework/account imports under the tested esbuild settings, but import succeeds in a clean local subprocess with only PATH and no server credentials.
new_observations.requirement: Declare existing locked runtime dependencies or make only a justified transport-helper extraction. Broad refactoring is unnecessary. Run the Nova adapter outside the provider/monitor daemon: the current monitor has that daemon socket, while the proposed adapter needs primary grant authority. Do not place primary database credentials into the provider runtime.

host.observed_architecture: Both existing daemon targets are ARM64. Docker Desktop: 10 assigned CPUs and 8319504384 memory bytes; Premium VM: 2 assigned CPUs and 3039596544 memory bytes.
host.interpretation: These are configured limits and current containers, not spare-capacity or load measurements. Existing runtime has an eight-minute configured stop grace; a new adapter needs its own supervised lifecycle. No existing process was stopped or reconfigured.

test_scope.method: Two pinned Node 22 containers, external network disabled, loopback HTTP permitted, synthetic admission and delayed in-memory terminal storage. Six diagnostic cases repeated on each architecture.
limits: No real Connect account, grant lookup, provider or database was exercised.
No full 300-second rerun this turn; prior edge/lifetime measurements remain historical.
No production client aggregator, resource adapter, keepalive wrapper or shutdown supervisor is implemented.
No new build artifact is accepted. The CORS dependency diagnostic ran separately on local Node 26.8.1.

minimum_implementation.change: Exact resource host/path validation; reuse current grant/entitlement/admission, executor and public projector; preserve CORS, OPTIONS and protected-resource metadata. No account cookies as Nova authority; fail closed before forwarding.

Track registered terminalWork, bridge correct upload/response aborts, flush authorized SSE headers, bound backpressure/keepalive, and drain before pool shutdown. Keep original 300000 ms execution and conservative finalization.

Opt into stream:true; stream-decode frames and accumulate allowlisted content under separate byte limits. Validate terminal reason plus DONE. Keep partial output explicitly unconfirmed; do not store GALX credentials in output or retry ambiguous work.

Retain the prior 360-second web artifact. Produce a new Hobby-compatible portal/web output with the long resource endpoint absent or fail-closed, and a separately identified native ARM64 resource package with explicit dependencies. Do not deploy a rewired old archive.

Verify disabled and wrong-host routing, complete authorization/entitlement/revocation matrix, source/package provenance, full-duration delayed/streamed/quiet responses, slow reader, cancellation, shutdown, capacity, duplicate/no-replay, buffer limits, browser/native results and public/private scans. Rollout remains separately authorized.

no_new_product_scope: No durable submit/poll queue or public result-retrieval API.
No changes to quota, provider-health classification, unknown semantics, identity, grants, pricing or historical records.
Current Nova duplicates return the recorded conflict without resubmission; the underlying execution attachment behavior is unchanged. Do not invent a public resume operation.

required_authority_placement.proposed: A constrained resource process/container on the existing general host, isolated from the Premium provider/desktop daemon. Same primary Connect database authority, no new account data store.
required_authority_placement.not_yet_proven: Exact database principal/configuration for the new adapter, host scheduling headroom and supervised restart acceptance. No new credential issuance or role changes occurred.

financial_and_eligibility.paid_upgrade: Declined; no purchase or recurring subscription added.
financial_and_eligibility.hobby: Short requests only, subject to the documented personal/non-commercial eligibility. This pass does not determine commercial eligibility.
financial_and_eligibility.fallback: Existing host may also serve web/Connect if required; that package/placement is not accepted by this observation.

action_status.ACT-044: Prior candidate closure only; replacement package must be reaccepted.
action_status.ACT-046: Prior disabled configuration closure only; new host must repeat the boundary proof.

references.claim: IncomingMessage close after completed upload differs from prematurely closed ServerResponse; write backpressure and drain are explicit.
Origin connection settings are distinct from the execution owner. The actual-edge timing proof remains in the earlier record.
